headline: High-risk shared-workspace and plugin-driven interaction: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and call MCP/OpenAPI tools while RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no stated isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can ingest application-defined files and call MCP/OpenAPI tools; RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no stated isolation or provenance controls. A shared filesystem or plugin bridge could let attacker-controlled content from one side influence the other. The exact bridge is not documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or MCP tool channel
IF RisingWave outputs are parsed by Semantic Kernel as instructions or tool arguments
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP tools for untrusted content paths
Add provenance tags before passing outputs between agents
Require allowlisted file paths for Semantic Kernel inputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel reads files, uses broad network egress, and handles plugin credentials; RisingWave touches data-engineering workloads and has no documented data-class limits. If both access the same workspace, file contents can flow into a third-party model or API. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default library usage, but the exact data classes are not documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing sensitive files
IF Semantic Kernel forwards those files to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Turn off networked model providers for sensitive runs
Use separate credentials per agent
Restrict Semantic Kernel file readers to a staging directory
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention and egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RisingWave is a database/stream-processing system, while Semantic Kernel can write files and call external tools. Even without explicit git or shell access, both can mutate shared application state through files, plugins, or downstream services. Because the shared mutable surface is inferred rather than directly documented, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application-defined files or shared memory store
IF a plugin or downstream service is used as a shared mutable resource
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Use per-agent namespaces in shared stores
Add file-locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is designed for function-calling against plugins, so it may treat upstream outputs as actionable inputs. RisingWave can produce data outputs that Semantic Kernel could render or route onward without verification. The pairwise pathway exists, but there is no direct evidence that either agent blindly trusts the other, so medium fits the documented interaction risk.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are fed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin arguments
IF Semantic Kernel acts on those outputs without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step
Require schema validation on all upstream outputs
Mark upstream content as untrusted in prompts
Limit downstream actions to read-only mode
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for RisingWave, while Semantic Kernel is a library with broad network egress and plugin credentials. The only concrete compliance concern is that application-defined files and external model/API calls could create policy gaps if sensitive data is routed through third parties. Because the mismatch is not explicit, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Semantic Kernel prompts or files
IF external providers are used without an approved DPA or residency review
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of external prompts
Use approved regional model endpoints
Document retention settings for plugins
Review data-flow diagrams before deployment
requires-engineering: add compliance gating for sensitive workloads
